name: arc-zero-block-cross-mask
description: Use when an ARC grid contains a 2x2 zero marker. Extend its two rows and columns as zero cross-lines, preserving 2s.
---

# ARC 2×2 Zero-Block Cross Mask

Use when an ARC-style grid contains a contiguous 2×2 block of zeros amid otherwise varied digits.

1. Locate the 2×2 zero block at rows `r,r+1` and columns `c,c+1`.
2. In the output, set every cell in rows `r,r+1` and columns `c,c+1` to `0` (the union forms a full-width/full-height cross).
3. Preserve any cell equal to `2` within those rows or columns; leave all cells outside the cross unchanged.
4. Keep the original grid dimensions.

The demonstrated rule leaves the marker's four zeroes intact, zeroes the two marker rows and columns across the whole grid, and keeps the `2` cells as exceptions.",
